welcome.desc: Answer a few questions about your health and habits. We’ll show which cancer screenings may apply to you, what to discuss with a clinician, and where to find care nearby.
welcome.trustPhone: Your answers stay on your phone

risk.title: Risk score calculator
risk.lead: A score for each cancer: how far your answers move you from average. Change an answer to see the scores move. It is not your chance of getting cancer.
risk.leadHelper: A score for each cancer: how far their answers move them from average. Change an answer to see the scores move. It is not their chance of getting cancer.
risk.biggestBody: {action} would move this from {a}× to {b}× average: “{band}.”
risk.noLever: What raises this is history, not habit. That makes the screening talk worth having.
risk.geneBody: A gene change you were born with matters far more than anything here. A genetic counselor can tell you what yours means.
risk.symptomTitle: You flagged a symptom for this one
risk.symptomBody: A symptom needs a visit, not a score. Your plan starts with it.
risk.thinBody: Fewer than half of the factors were answered, so no score is shown. Fill them in under Change answers.

surveilTitle.cervical: Your follow-up tests decide this one

surveilBody.liver: Long-term hepatitis B or C puts liver cancer risk far above average, so a score would not help. Ask a clinician if you need regular liver checks. Treating hepatitis lowers the risk.
surveilBody.cervical: An abnormal Pap or HPV test means follow-up tests, set by the result. A score would not help. Go to every follow-up visit.

risk.diaryOn: Diet uses your food diary ({n} days logged).
risk.diaryOff: Diet uses your check answers. Log 3 days in the food diary to use real amounts.
risk.ageTitle: Age is not in these scores
risk.ageBody: Age is the biggest driver of cancer risk. It is the starting point, not part of the score. A 35-year-old at 2× has far less risk than a 70-year-old at 1×. Compare yourself with people your own age.
risk.methodTitle: How the score is worked out
risk.methodBody: Each factor has a relative risk from a named study. The factors for a cancer are multiplied, as in the Harvard Cancer Risk Index. The result is the score. Skipped answers are left out, not counted as healthy. There is no AI here.
readNotes: Your score shows if your answers raise or lower your risk. It compares you with an average person your age and sex.
Each factor is counted on its own, so the score is a guide, not an exact number.
Every figure comes from a published study. You can see each source below.
It counts what the health check asks about. A clinician can look at more of your story.
It cannot say whether you will get cancer. Screening and a talk with a clinician are the next steps.
risk.disclaimer: This is for learning, not a clinical risk test. A clinician can use tools that know more about you.

policy.intro: This policy covers the FutureVitals app. It is written to be read. Every line describes what the app really does.

sections.p: FutureVitals is an app for learning about cancer screening. It does not diagnose. It is not a medical device, and it does not replace a clinician.

sections.h: What the app stores, and where
sections.p: Your check answers, your plan, saved places, your food diary, your language and theme, and a ZIP code if you type one. Products you look up are kept too, so they work offline. All of it stays on your phone. There is no account and no server that receives it.

Only one thing, and only if you use the scanner. Most products are in a list inside the app, so looking them up sends nothing. For a barcode that is not in that list, the app sends the number to Open Food Facts, a free public food list. No answers, plan, place or ID go with it. Links you tap open in your browser. They send nothing from the app.
If you tap “Use my location,” your phone’s position is used once, in memory, to sort nearby places. It is not saved and not sent. ZIP codes are looked up on your phone.
The scanner uses the camera on your phone to read a barcode or an ingredient list. Pictures are read on your phone and are not saved or sent.
On Android, the app keeps your data out of phone backups. If your iPhone backs up to iCloud, that backup can include it, as it does for every app.
No analytics. No advertising. No trackers. No selling or sharing of data, because we do not receive any.
“Delete my plan” takes away the plan and its answers. “Delete my answers from this device” takes away all of it. So does taking the app off your phone.
The app is for adults. It collects nothing from anyone.
If this policy changes, you will get the new one in an app update. The date at the top will change too.

about.headline: About FutureVitals
about.reviewerPending: Not yet assigned. Needed before public release.
about.dataBody: The scanner uses Open Food Facts, a free food list that anyone can edit. The app holds a copy of part of it: products sold in the U.S. That copy is shared under the same Open Database License.
about.disclaimerBody: FutureVitals is for learning. It does not diagnose, does not give a chance of getting cancer, and does not replace a clinician. Guidelines change. Clinic details can change, so call before you go.
about.feedbackNote: Opens your email app. Please do not send medical details.
about.helperNote: For health workers and helpers who fill in the check for others. It clears the answers after each person.

scan.title: Product scanner
scan.lead: Scan a food package. See what studies say about what is in it.
scan.searchPlaceholder: A product, a brand, or a food like “hot dogs”
scan.privacyNote: The camera runs on your phone. Most products are found on your phone. For the rest, only the barcode number is sent.
scan.pointCamera: Hold the barcode in the box. Then tap Take picture.
scan.noCamera: The camera is not available. You can type the barcode instead.
scan.denied: Camera access is off. You can type the barcode instead.
scan.notFound: We could not find this product. Take a photo of its ingredients instead.
scan.offline: You are offline, and this product is not in the app’s list. Products in the list, and ones scanned before, still work.
scan.fromCache: Saved on this phone from an earlier scan.
scan.ocrLoading: Getting the text reader ready (first time only)…
scan.ocrCheck: Check the text we read. Fix any mistakes, then tap Check.
scan.ocrFailed: We could not read that. Try again in better light, or type the ingredients.

labels.none: No cancer evidence for these ingredients

reasons.group1: It contains an IARC Group 1 or 2A item.
reasons.nova4: It is ultra-processed, with added sugar or salt above WHO limits.
reasons.processed: It is a processed food with no Group 1 or 2A item.
reasons.group2b: It has an additive IARC lists as possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B).
reasons.wcrf: It has a food that WCRF says is probably a cause of cancer.
reasons.clean: Nothing in it is on the IARC or WCRF risk lists.

grade.title: Ingredient grade
grade.none: We found nothing in it that is linked to cancer.
grade.missing: No grade. There is no ingredient list to check.
grade.weightItem: Ultra-processed, high in sugar or salt
how: Each item linked to cancer adds points. Stronger proof adds more.
The grade counts items. It does not know how much of each is in the food, or how much you eat.
It is a guide for comparing foods. It is not your own risk.

scan.offNote: This list comes from Open Food Facts. Anyone can edit it. Check it against the package.
scan.flagged: Ingredients on IARC or WCRF lists
scan.sugar: Added sugar above the WHO limit
scan.note: This shows what the evidence says about ingredients, not a risk from one product. Amount and frequency matter more than any single item.
scan.localTitle: Searches the products and ingredients in the app. Sends nothing.
scan.noMatch: No match in the app’s product or ingredient lists.
scan.notInList: This barcode is not in the app’s product list, and this preview cannot look it up online. Type the ingredients from the package instead.
scan.builtIn: {n} products sold in the U.S. are in the app. Looking one up sends nothing.
scan.fromList: From the product list in the app
scan.photoNote: Your phone’s camera takes a photo. The barcode is read on your phone, and the photo is not saved.
scan.photoInstead: Choose a photo of the barcode
scan.readingDigits: Reading the numbers under the barcode…
scan.noBarcodeTitle: No barcode found in the photo
scan.noBarcode: Hold the phone closer, keep the barcode flat and in good light, and try again. Or type the numbers under it.
scan.ocrBarcode: Looking for a barcode in the photo…
scan.barcodeInPhoto: Found the barcode in your photo.
scan.unreadableTitle: We could not read the ingredients
scan.unreadable: The photo was not clear enough to read. We will not guess, so nothing was checked.
photoTips: Photograph the back of the package, where the ingredient list is.
Fill the photo with just the ingredient list.
Hold the phone steady and flat to the package, in good light.
Flatten a shiny or curved bag so the words do not bend or glare.
